metadata.title: Separable Codes for Time and Decision in Human Temporal Perception - Code
metadata.description:
This repository contains the Python analysis scripts associated with the study "Separable Codes for Time and Decision in Human Temporal Perception" (Silvestrin et al., https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.28.721130).

The code implements the full analysis pipeline, from behavioral modeling to multivariate EEG decoding and statistical inference. Scripts are numbered to reflect the analysis order.

  • 01_BehaviourModels.py — Fits the Internal Reference Model (IRM) to behavioral data, including grid search over learning rate parameters (κ_within, κ_between), likelihood ratio tests comparing nested models, and integration of IRM estimates with EEG metadata for downstream analyses.
  • 02a_MVPA_Estimates.py — Time-resolved LDA decoding of category (shorter vs. longer) and duration (0.5 s vs. 1.0 s) information from offset-locked EEG epochs, using 5-fold cross-validation.
  • 02b_MVPA_Figures.py — Regression of logit-transformed classifier probabilities on categorical and temporal predictors across time, with permutation-based group-level inference (tmax, 5,000 permutations) and figure generation.
  • 02c_MVPA_TG.py — Temporal generalization analysis assessing how decoding patterns generalize across time points.
  • 03a_MVPA_TOIs_Estimates.py — Window-based MVPA decoding within three pre-defined time windows of interest (TOIs): pre-offset (−200 to −50 ms), early (150–300 ms), and late (300–450 ms) relative to interval offset.
  • 03b_MVPA_TOIs_OrthoTests.py — Orthogonality tests between category and duration neural representations, including cross-dimensional generalization and classifier weight-pattern correlation analyses.
  • 03c_MVPA_TOIs_DecisionalResults.py — Regression of TOI-level decoder evidence on behavioral predictors, and model comparison between categorical label and distance-from-internal-reference as predictors of neural category evidence.
  • 04_ROI_analysis.py — Region-of-interest ERP analysis using time windows and electrode clusters derived from the MVPA results.

metadata.title: Bilinearity Preserving Algebraic Flux Correction: code and data
metadata.description: Julia code reproducing the numerical experiments of S. S. Dash and A. Jha, Bilinearity Preserving Algebraic Flux Correction. Implements the algebraic flux correction scheme for convection–diffusion–reaction equations with the limiter of Barrenechea, John and Knobloch for an arbitrary nodal parameter, covering the bilinearity-preserving choice derived in the paper and the original linearity-preserving one.

metadata.title: amr-clonalshare: measuring how much of antimicrobial resistance travels with the clone
metadata.description:
Python package and command-line tool that estimates the share of variance in an antimicrobial resistance phenotype carried by the lineages of a bacterial collection, from a lineage label and a susceptibility call or a recorded dilution, and refuses the estimate where the collection cannot support one. One collection admits three quantities and the package reports them apart: the lineage-membership share, what a rule scored out of sample reaches, with a lineage bootstrap; the design-corrected component ratio of the same collection, with an interval exact under the Gaussian one-way model by inversion of a noncentral F; and the superpopulation share for the species, with a chi-square layer on the number of lineages. Each is scored against its own truth on 135 simulated cells from five lineages to a thousand, and each sits behind a gate that refuses where the collection cannot identify the quantity or the residuals contradict the law the interval assumes, the coverage of each having been measured. A binary share is restated on the latent scale of the threshold model beside the observed scale. The lineage label may be a sequence type, a core-genome or SNP cluster, or a serovar, so the same estimate can be read at two typing resolutions.

For a difference in non-wild-type prevalence between two collections it applies the Kitagawa decomposition to split the difference into a lineage-composition component and a within-lineage rate component, with a shared-support gate calibrated against measured interval coverage, a test for lineage labels that are differentially and informatively missing, and Benjamini-Yekutieli control within each component family of the antimicrobial panel, valid whatever the dependence between agents.

Ships a Streptococcus suis case study (677 isolates, 650 porcine and 27 human, with full data provenance) read at population-cluster and at sequence-type resolution, together with a 720,000-decomposition calibration study and a head-to-head comparison against lineage-adjusted logistic regression. The package reads two tables and never a genome.

A susceptibility panel is read at its recorded resolution: a dichotomised call and a recorded dilution are both intervals on the log2 concentration scale and enter one interval likelihood, so the input mode changes how much an observation carries rather than what is estimated. The interval is exact where every reading is a point and calibrated by simulation where a reading is an interval, and the tested wells are taken from the recorded values unless the panel is supplied. Each share carries an e-value; a run that declares the intake each isolate arrived in also carries the running product over intakes, a test supermartingale that may be read after any intake, with the panel decision taken on the log scale so that evidence too strong for a float is still evidence. False-discovery control across the panel holds under arbitrary dependence.

The attribution is exercised outside the shipped cohorts on fifty organisms of one NCBI Pathogen Detection release, each taken at the release accession the retrieval recorded: every agent of every cohort that reaches the estimator leaves one record, estimated or refused with the condition that failed, 192 cells are estimated in twelve species and 44 admitted by the support gate in six, and every cell carries a permuted-label control. The Streptococcus suis cohort is read at three definitions of a lineage, population cluster, serotype and sequence type, with the reference label rerun on each other label's own isolates so that the label is separated from the collection.

A veterinary arm cuts the same source by host species and by sampling matrix and runs every cell at two definitions of a lineage, the Pathogen Detection SNP cluster and the serovar, with the permuted-label control at both. The pair is reported rather than one number, because the share a cohort carries is a function of the resolution at which a lineage is defined, and a laboratory that serotypes holds a different resolution from one that clusters genomes.

metadata.title: SPARQ: spiking physics-in-the-loop autonomous reinforcement triage of quantum emitters
metadata.description:
Inference release: the toolbox now covers all three schools honestly. The parametric bootstrap propagates shot noise through the full pipeline, the Wilks profile likelihood gives model-based frequentist intervals -- and bayesian_g2 adds the EXACT finite-count Bayesian posterior of the model-free quantity experimental papers quote first: the raw central-window g2, the zero-delay coincidence rate over the flat level.

New in sparq.bayes

  • bayesian_g2 / G2Posterior: with independent Gamma priors on the central and reference per-bin Poisson rates (Jeffreys a = 1/2 by default), the conjugate posteriors are closed-form Gammas, and the posterior of their RATIO is a scaled beta-prime law -- density, CDF, quantiles, equal-tailed credible intervals, mean/median/mode, and the triage verdict probability P[g2 < 1/2 | data] are exact expressions in four counts. No sampling, no optimizer, no asymptotics. Acquisition time and detection rates cancel in the ratio, so none need be supplied.
  • The estimand, stated plainly: a window average sits ON TOP of the antibunching dip, so it upper-bounds the true g2(0); that is a property of the quantity, not of the inference, and the docstring says so. Dip-shape-aware estimation of g2(0) itself stays with profile_likelihood_ci -- the two tools answer different questions.

Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated)

  • The hand-built density, CDF and quantile function agree with scipy.stats.betaprime -- an independent implementation -- to 1e-12, with the CDF-of-quantile identity closed to 1e-10.
  • The density integrates to one and reproduces the closed-form posterior mean by quadrature; the mode is a verified stationary point.
  • The closed form equals a direct numerical marginalization of the exact Poisson likelihood over the nuisance rate -- an integral the module itself never evaluates.
  • Seeded Monte-Carlo ratios of Gamma draws match the distribution function to statistical tolerance.
  • On twin-generated histograms the 95 percent credible interval covers the true central-bin ratio at its nominal rate, and the posterior mean converges to the high-count ratio.
  • The verdict probability orders single- against two-emitter sites correctly (P > 0.9 vs P < 0.5 at the tested brightness).
  • Malformed inputs are refused: wrong grid length, even windows, negative counts, improper priors, empty or overlapping windows.

61 tests across Python 3.9-3.13 (ML tests skip without torch). Install: pip install -U sparq-triage.

metadata.title: absnoise: Andreev-bound-state occupation noise and detector budgets for proximity Josephson junctions
metadata.description:
Characterization release: the shipped recipes are Jung et al.'s six junctions; yours needs its own (Ic0, Tc*, tau) before any budget in this package applies to it. The standard measurement -- critical current versus temperature -- determines exactly those parameters, and fit_ic_curve implements the fit against the package's own short-junction ensemble.

New in absnoise.icfit

  • fit_ic_curve: bounded nonlinear least squares of Ic(T) = Ic0 M(T; Tc, tau)/M(0) with the BCS gap solved from the gap equation (no tanh shortcut). Ic0 absorbs channel count and series factors; Tc sets the gap scale; tau is identified by the SHAPE of the suppression -- transparent junctions keep their supercurrent to higher T/Tc than tunnel junctions. With measurement sigmas: exact known-noise covariance plus a chi-square consistency check. A curve that never leaves the low-temperature plateau triggers a warning that Tc and tau are weakly determined, instead of a well-formatted result implying a well-determined one.
  • IcFit.to_recipe: packages the fit with your measured geometry (xi, L, W, Vbg, Rn -- values an Ic(T) curve does not determine, so the method does not pretend to) as a Recipe, and every thermometry and calorimetry budget in the package applies to your junction directly.
  • ic_model: the forward model exposed on its own, with the closed-form zero-temperature maximizing phase sin^2(phi*/2) = (1 - sqrt(1 - tau))/tau used for normalization.

Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated)

  • The closed-form T = 0 maximizing phase equals a dense phase-grid maximum to 1e-8 across transparencies from 0.05 to 0.99.
  • The fit's forward model agrees with the package's independent ShortJunction.Ic implementation to machine precision on every shipped recipe and temperature tested.
  • Noise-free synthetic curves return the generating (Ic0, Tc, tau) to 1e-5 or better, with chi-square consistent with exact data.
  • Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted parameters is compatible with the reported sigmas, and the recovered Tc is unbiased at the tested noise level.
  • Malformed and unconstraining data are refused or warned about (too few points, no sigmas with n = 4, negative currents, non-finite values, plateau-only temperature ranges).
  • A fitted recipe re-enters the pipeline: the calibrated ShortJunction built from it reproduces the input curve to 1e-4.

62 tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U absnoise.
metadata.notes: If this software is useful in your work, please cite it.

metadata.title: ramansep: two-mode separation of strain and carrier density in 2D-material Raman maps
metadata.description:
Calibration release: the package's no-shipped-coefficients policy finally comes with the tool that closes the loop. Every shipped set carries the caveat that lever arms depend on material, mode pair, excitation and substrate; calibrate_lever_arms turns reference measurements you control -- a strain-stage sweep, a gated sweep, any points with known (strain, density) -- into your own fitted coefficient matrix, with uncertainties and provenance.

New in ramansep.calibration

  • calibrate_lever_arms: weighted least-squares fit of the (m, 2) lever-arm matrix, one linear problem per mode on the shared reference design. With shift sigmas the parameter covariance is the exact known-noise Gauss-Markov result and a per-mode chi-square consistency check comes back with it; without sigmas the covariance uses the residual variance, which is why that path refuses fewer than three reference points instead of inventing an error bar.
  • Identifiability refused, not fudged: reference states collinear in the (strain, density) plane (a strain-only sweep, or gating that strains proportionally) cannot separately determine the two arms of any mode -- the fit raises with an explanation instead of returning one of infinitely many minimizers.
  • CalibrationResult.coefficients() packages a two-mode calibration as a ModeCoefficients with a MANDATORY provenance string; result.K feeds MultiModeModel directly for m > 2.

Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated)

  • Noise-free shifts from a known matrix are recovered to machine precision, with zero estimated uncertainty.
  • The hand-built normal-equation solution agrees with an independent QR solve (numpy.linalg.lstsq on the whitened system) to 1e-10.
  • The orthogonal unit design {(1,0), (0,1)} with unit sigmas has EXACTLY the identity parameter covariance -- the closed form, not an approximation.
  • Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted arms matches the reported sigmas.
  • Degenerate and malformed reference sets raise (collinear designs, n = 1, n = 2 without sigmas, non-positive sigmas, non-finite shifts).
  • The full round trip -- calibrate on synthetic references, package the coefficients, invert forward-generated maps through SeparationModel -- returns the input strain and density maps to 1e-10.

50 tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U ramansep.

metadata.title: hamop: bands, DOS, Kubo optical conductivity and NEGF transmission from one tight-binding Hamiltonian
metadata.description:
Local spectroscopy release: the NEGF layer now answers where in a device the spectral weight sits and how the current flows through it, not only how much transmits.

New in hamop.negf

  • device_greens: the retarded device Green function G(E) of the partitioned two-probe system (leads folded in through their Sancho-Rubio self-energies), the quantity every local observable below is built from -- returned with the broadening matrices, so users can construct their own correlators.
  • device_ldos: the site- and orbital-resolved local density of states from the spectral function A = i(G - G+), overlap (nonorthogonal) bases included.
  • bond_currents: the energy-resolved bond-current map J_ij of Paulsson and Brandbyge (Phys. Rev. B 76, 115117 (2007)) for carriers injected from either lead -- the microscopic current paths whose cuts recover the Landauer transmission.

Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated)

  • The finite-eta spectral identity i(G - G+) = G (Gamma_L + Gamma_R + 2 eta S) G+ holds to machine precision -- overlap matrix included -- so the LDOS is exactly consistent with the same Green function the transmission uses.
  • A closed device reproduces the exact closed form: its LDOS equals the sum of eta-Lorentzians over its own eigenvalues, site weights included.
  • On a translation-uniform ribbon the LDOS is exactly uniform along the transport direction.
  • Bond currents obey Kirchhoff's law at every interior site to machine precision; every transverse cut through the device carries exactly the transmission T(E); injection and drain contacts source and sink exactly +T and -T.
  • Inside a band gap every bond current vanishes.

124 closed-form-anchored tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U hamop.
metadata.notes: If this software is useful in your work, please cite it.

metadata.title: eGamma: an expanded Gamma distribution library for Python
metadata.description:
eGamma implements the expanded Gamma distribution: a three-parameter Gamma distribution whose scale parameter is allowed to be negative, so that the density is reflected about its location parameter and can represent left-skewed as well as right-skewed data. In that form the family is Pearson Type III, expressed in the Gamma distribution's own shape, scale and location parameters, so that existing Gamma routines can be reused.

The library provides the density, cumulative distribution and quantile functions, random variates, and the moments of the distribution — mean, mode, median, variance, standard deviation, skewness and excess kurtosis. Parameters can be obtained in two ways. They can be fitted to a sample, by maximum likelihood or by the method of moments. Alternatively they can be fitted to a three-point estimate, where a low, most likely and high value are supplied and the outer two are interpreted at a chosen pair of symmetric percentiles, the 10th and 90th by default. The three-point routine is intended for probabilistic cost and schedule analysis, where estimates elicited from experts must be turned into distributions that a Monte Carlo simulation can sample.

Conformance test vectors giving inputs and fitted parameters at full double precision are distributed with the package as a machine-readable file, and are exercised by the test suite.

Source code: github.com/FrodeDrevland/egamma
Package: pypi.org/project/egamma
Documentation: frodedrevland.github.io/egamma
